failures.evidence: A block node's id is `<ref_key>#<block id>` (document_blocks.node_id, unique), and the 256-byte bound covers only the block id, so a long reference key still overflows the key. Uploading a document named with 2680 random hex characters (`dispatch artifact --issue CORE-3 --name <2680 hex>.md --path f`): main 81a3b5ef (port 8841) stores version 1; the head (port 8801) answers 500, log 'record the blocks version 1 of … changed: ERROR: index row size 2744 exceeds btree version 4 maximum 2704 for index "document_blocks_node_id_key"'. After rolling main's database onto the head build, the document main stored cannot be edited (`dispatch doc-edit` → 500, same index), and the block-index loop logs 'block index skipped a document it could not index' for it on every pass. A 2690-character name fails on main too (artifacts_ref_key_key), so the gap is the ~36-260 bytes the node id adds. Red test: TestADocumentWhoseReferenceKeyLeavesNoRoomForABlockIDIsStillWritten in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/block_id_bound_test.go (commit 8eda5b76); `cd packages/envoy && go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run TestADocumentWhoseReferenceKeyLeavesNoRoomForABlockIDIsStillWritten -count=1 -v` fails with 'upload a document named with 2680 characters: status=500 … want 201 as main answers'. With a 2000-character name the same test passes, so its later assertions hold. The implementer's comment dispatch://INFRA-366/comment/85ee2d5a-64ec-4fe7-9a2e-2c55ee09f44f names this gap as outside the issue; it is a regression this pull request introduces (main writes these documents), unlike the refs_pkey overflow there, which main already has.
